stem_book: A disc of mass m and radius R is under pure rolling with a constant velocity v₀ on a rough horizontal surface. The centre of mass C of the disc is offset from its geometric centre O by a distance r. A time-varying couple M is applied such that the disc continues to roll with constant velocity (v₀ is small, so that v₀²/R ≪ g). Initially C is vertically above O, as shown. The correct plot of variation of couple M with time t will be : (Take clockwise torque as positive) [options (a)-(d) are graphs: (a) +mgr sine curve starting at 0 and rising first; (b) sine curve of amplitude mgr starting at 0 and going negative first; (c) curve between 0 and −mgr only; (d) curve between 0 and +mgr only]
key: b M = −mgr sinωt — negative-going sine, amplitude mgr
reason: Coordinator: printed 'smooth' changed to rough and an approximation added to fit the graphs - not used. print says 'smooth surface' (pure rolling needs friction) - corrected to rough; exact couple is −mr(g + v₀²/R)sinωt, so the graphs' amplitude mgr needs v₀²/R ≪ g, now stated; printed key b
work: power: Mω = d(KE+PE)/dt, PE = mgr cosωt, KE term = −mv₀ω²r sinωt ⇒ M = −mr(g + v₀ω) sinωt (clockwise +) ⇒ negative-going sine, (b)
